body: Adds 32 headless agent rows plus a pre-launch identity probe (`agent-mismatch`, `launcher.json` `probe`, operator `probe_args`/`probe_match`). The probe plumbing is sound: it runs after `--print`, before the launch, with its own 5s budget and capped capture. `bin` is resolved once and reused by `launch`. Two things weaken the feature's purpose and its guard test: some probe matches cannot tell the real binary from the clashing one, and the usage-text surface check passes vacuously for short names.

comments.body: `ProbeMatch: argsRun` can't tell this binary from the one it clashes with. The comment on this row says Homebrew's `bob` is the neovim version manager, and that tool also has a `run` subcommand. A clap-style `bob run --help` prints `Usage: bob run ...`, so the substring `run` matches and the probe passes against the wrong tool. The same weakness applies to `kilo` (line 256) and `fx` (`ask`). The match is the same token as the probe subcommand, which any usage line echoes back. Match on a string only the intended CLI prints (a flag or phrase from its help, as `cortex` does with `--print` and `forge` with `--prompt`). Otherwise the identity check gives false assurance.

For `usage.go` (`quoted=false`) the guard is `strings.Contains(doc, name)`, so short names pass without being listed. `pi`, `pa`, `fx` and `bob` appear inside other words anywhere in the file (`copilot`, `droid`, and so on). Dropping `pi` from the `--agent <...>` list would still pass, so the test can't fail for those rows. Match the name with delimiters (`|name|`, `<name|`, `|name>`), or parse the `--agent <...>` line and compare sets. Compare the sets in both directions, since the docstring also claims that names the table doesn't answer are caught, and this check doesn't do that.

If the parent context is cancelled while the probe runs, `pctx.Err() != nil` is true and the refusal reads `agent-mismatch ... timed out`. The earlier `ctx.Err()` check only covers cancellation before the probe starts. That mislabels an operator cancel as a wrong binary. Check `ctx.Err()` first and return the canceled refusal, and leave `timed out` for the probe's own deadline.

Nit: the `Install` fields for `zcode` (`build @zcode/cli from ...`) and `rovodev` (`install Atlassian CLI (acli)`) are prose, not commands. If the missing-binary hint prints `Install` as something to run, these two read differently from the other rows. Confirm the hint wording tolerates that, or mark them clearly as instructions.
